figure: Figure 10.1 (TP / PP / DP, three stacked panels)
issue: The in-figure color key 'weights (blue)' is honored only in panel A. In panel B the model's layers are drawn as unpatterned white sub-boxes, and in panel C the model is drawn as the orange 'full model (replica)' GPU box; neither B nor C contains any blue. A color reader applying the legend expects the model/weights to be blue in all three panels, so the key is inconsistent with 2 of 3 panels. issue: The figure has no numbered caption on the page where it appears. The figure is followed only by a 'Figure note (grayscale): ...' line, which is a note about the color key, not a caption. Verify by searching the built PDF for 'Figure 10.1' and confirming the page index equals the page index of the figure.

issue: Panel B asserts a pipeline bubble but never draws one. The annotation under the GPU row reads 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain - pipeline-wide', and the body prose on the same page says 'an idle bubble appears as the pipeline fills and drains'. Nothing in the diagram shows an idle stage, an unfilled time slot, or any time axis, so the one property that distinguishes PP from TP and DP in the prose is invisible in the figure.
evidence: Printed p. 173, panel B: three GPU boxes in a row with two arrows between them and the annotation 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain - pipeline-wide' beneath. There is no bubble glyph, no dashed 'idle' segment, and no fill/drain timeline. A reader who has never seen a pipeline diagram cannot tell what the annotation refers to; a reader who has can only take it on trust.
acceptance_test: Panel B must depict the bubble - for example a small fill/drain timeline inset beneath the GPU row showing stage occupancy over time with the idle interval hatched and labeled, or an explicitly drawn idle segment inside one stage box - and the annotation must point at what it names. Alternatively, remove the annotation and the corresponding prose clause. Acceptance: a reader who has never seen a pipeline diagram can point to the idle region and say which stage is idle during fill and which during drain.

issue: Panel B does not depict the thing it claims to split. Panels A and C each show the split object explicitly - a weight matrix W in A, batch shards A/B in C - but panel B, titled 'splits the layer stack', shows only three generic boxes labeled 'GPU 0', 'GPU 1', 'GPU 2'. The layer stack, the stage boundaries, and the mapping of layers to stages are all absent, so the panel's title is not supported by anything the eye can see.
evidence: Printed p. 173, panel B: three orange dashed boxes labeled GPU 0 / GPU 1 / GPU 2, two arrows, the label 'activations -> P2P at stage boundaries', and the note 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain - pipeline-wide'. No layer-stack bar, no layer ranges, no stage partition. Compare panel A, which draws 'one layer's weight matrix W' as a bar, and panel C, which draws 'batch shard A' / 'batch shard B' as bars. The asymmetry is the defect: the figure's comparative job is to show what each strategy partitions, and panel B is the only one that does not.
acceptance_test: Panel B must draw the layer stack as a partitioned object - e.g. a vertical bar divided into three contiguous segments labeled with the layer ranges they carry (layers 0-22 / 23-45 / 46-69 for the canonical 70B model, or a generic 'layers 0-n1 / n1-n2 / n2-N') - with each segment visually mapped to its GPU and the stage boundaries aligned with the P2P arrows. Acceptance: the reader can state which layers each GPU holds without reading prose.

confidence: medium (fill state must be confirmed at full resolution)

All three GPU boxes must carry identical orange cross-hatch fill, unless the empty box is deliberately the drawn bubble - in which case it must be labeled as such (see FIG-10.1-02) and the legend must accommodate it. issue: Panel A draws the weight matrix as a single undivided bar with two arrows leaving it, which reads as the same matrix being handed to both GPUs (replication) rather than being partitioned across them (sharding). The panel title says 'splits one layer's weights' and the caption says 'Tensor parallel shards one layer's weight matrix across GPUs', but the drawn object is never divided.
evidence: Printed p. 173, panel A: one blue hatched bar labeled 'one layer's weight matrix W' spanning both GPUs, with two blue arrows descending to 'GPU 0' and 'GPU 1'. The arrows leave from different x positions, which weakly hints at a partition, but no boundary, no shard labels, and no 'W[:, :d/2]' / 'W[:, d/2:]]' annotation is present. The figure therefore does not distinguish TP from naive weight replication - the single most consequential distinction in the panel.
acceptance_test: The bar must be visibly partitioned into two labeled shards (e.g. 'W[:, 0:d/2]' and 'W[:, d/2:d]'), each routed to exactly one GPU, with the partition boundary drawn. Acceptance: a reader can answer 'is the weight matrix copied or divided?' from the figure alone, and the answer is unambiguous.

issue: The body prose identifies replicated activations as a defining property of TP ('activations are replicated'), but the figure shows no activations at all. The only blue element is the weight bar, so the figure depicts TP as a scheme in which only weights move. A reader could reasonably infer that TP's communication is weight traffic rather than activation traffic, which inverts the actual cost structure.
evidence: Printed p. 173, panel A and the paragraph immediately below the figure: 'Tensor parallel shards one layer's weight matrix across GPUs - activations are replicated, and each GPU's partial sums are all-reduced...'. Panel A contains no activation element; the red box is labeled 'all-reduce partial sums -> full output', which is the output side, not the input side.
acceptance_test: Panel A must show the replicated input activation (a neutral-filled bar labeled 'input activation x (replicated to every GPU)') feeding both GPUs, visually distinct from the weight shards and from the red comms element. Acceptance: the figure shows both the replicated input and the reduced output, so the reader can see that TP's per-layer traffic is activation traffic.

issue: Panel C shows no weights, so the property that distinguishes DP from TP - that every GPU holds a full copy of the model - is not visible.
